==Problem 5==

Casey went on a road trip that covered <imath>100</imath> miles, stopping only for a lunch break along the way. The trip took <imath>3</imath> hours in total and her average speed while driving was <imath>40</imath> miles per hour. In minutes, how long was the lunch break?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }15 \qquad \textbf{(B) }30 \qquad \textbf{(C) }40 \qquad \textbf{(D) }45 \qquad \textbf{(E) }60</imath>

==Solution==
The average speed is <imath>\frac{ \text{ Total distance } }{ \text{ Total time } }</imath>, or <imath>\frac{100}{3-t}</imath>. Thus <imath>\frac{100}{3-t} = 40 \Rightarrow 3-t = \frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{2}</imath>, which is <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(B) } 30}</imath> minutes.

~OlympiadMaster

nah we can just do it like this. <imath>100</imath> miles at <imath>40</imath> miles per hour means we can do <imath>1</imath> mile in <imath>1.5</imath> minutes. so we multiply <imath>100</imath> by <imath>1.5</imath> to get <imath>150</imath> minutes or <imath>2</imath> hours and <imath>30</imath> minutes. (this is how long it took her to drive, and if the total time is three hours we do <imath>3</imath> minus <imath>2.5</imath> to get our answer <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(B) } 30}</imath> minutes.

==Solution 2==

Average speed is total distance over total time. Thus, the total time spent driving is <imath>t</imath> and the total distance is <imath>100</imath>, the average speed is <imath>100/t = 40</imath>. Solving, we have that <imath>t = 100/40 = 10/4 = 5/2</imath> hours, or <imath>2</imath> hours and <imath>30</imath> minutes. She drove for <imath>3</imath> hours, and thus her lunch break was <imath>\boxed{30}</imath> minutes.

~Pinotation

==Solution 3==

If the trip took <imath>3</imath> hours in total and her average speed was <imath>40</imath> miles per hour, we know she would have traveled <imath>120</imath> miles. Since she only traveled <imath>100</imath> miles with a lunch break, she would have traveled <imath>20</imath> miles if she didn't have a lunch break. Since her average speed was <imath>40</imath> miles per hour, the lunch break took <imath>60*\frac{20}{40}</imath> minutes. So the answer is <imath>\boxed{30}</imath> minutes.

~FJH07

==Solution 4==
Since Casey drove <imath> 100 </imath> miles at a constant rate of <imath> 40 </imath> mph, we can say it took her <imath> 100/40 = 2.5 </imath> hours to drive to his/her destination WITHOUT a break. The problem mentioned the trip took <imath> 3 </imath> hours, so <imath> 3 - 2.5 </imath> hours yields a total of <imath> 0.5 </imath> hours or <imath> 30 </imath> minutes, so the answer is <imath>\boxed{ \textbf{(B) } 30}</imath>.

~Ingeniouspeacock36

==Solution 5==

Using dimensional analysis, her time spent driving is
<cmath> 100 \text{ miles}\cdot \frac{ 1 \text{ hour} }{ 40 \text{ miles} } = 2.5 \text{ hours}. </cmath>
Therefore, she spent <imath>3 - 2.5 = 0.5 \text{ hours}</imath> during her lunch break or
<cmath> 0.5 \text{ hours} \cdot \frac{60 \text{ minutes}}{1 \text{ hour}} = \boxed{ \textbf{(B) } 30} \text{ minutes}.</cmath>

~Blosp
